name: Hailuo AI
tagline: Text-to-video and image-to-video generation using MiniMax models

pricing.basis: paid plan; billing basis requires review
pricing.native: Public paid plan exists; amount not safely recovered
pricing.notes: The official pricing URL is recorded, but a stable current amount was not safely recoverable in this pass. Do not publish a number until rechecked.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: Maximum 3 queued jobs and 1 parallel job; watermarked output; recurring free-credit quantity is not published.

tiers.name: Standard
tiers.limits: 1,000 subscription credits per billing period; paid queue allows up to 5 queued jobs and 2 parallel jobs.
tiers.notes: The annual-effective price is published in an official July 2026 article; the monthly price is published in Hailuo's payment policy.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: 4,500 subscription credits per billing period; up to 5 queued jobs and 2 parallel jobs.
tiers.notes: The annual-effective price is published in an official July 2026 article; the monthly price is published in Hailuo's payment policy.

tiers.name: Master
tiers.limits: 10,000 subscription credits in the payment policy; an official July 2026 article says 10,500.
tiers.notes: Official sources disagree on whether the allowance is 10,000 or 10,500 credits.

tiers.name: Ultra
tiers.limits: 12,000 subscription credits; includes the benefits inherited from the former Unlimited offer.
tiers.notes: A current annual total was not exposed in the official sources checked.

tiers.name: Max
tiers.limits: 20,000 subscription credits, then unlimited Hailuo-01/Hailuo-02 Relax Mode generation.
tiers.notes: A current annual total was not exposed in the official sources checked.

pricing.freeTierCaps: Watermarked output, maximum 3 queued jobs and 1 parallel job; the official pages do not publish the recurring free-credit quantity.
pricing.billingTerms: monthly subscriptions; annual pricing is published for Standard, Pro and Master, while current annual totals for Ultra and Max were not verifiable
pricing.hiddenCosts: Subscription credits expire at the end of each billing period and do not roll over. Extra credits cost $1 per 70 credits and expire on December 31 of the second calendar year after purchase; welcome credits expire after 3 days.

verdictSummary: Do not mistake the interface for the product. Hailuo AI's durable value is proprietary model, inference, safety, which a solo one-shot build cannot reproduce responsibly. The prompt therefore builds only the closest honest personal consolation tool.
coreLoopDIY: Build the closest honest personal AI video generation workflow using one user-selected local or API model, job history, preview, and export.
diyTimeEstimate: not a true replacement; consolation build in one to two days
replacementScope: consolation build only; the paid product's moat remains
requirements: GPU-capable machine or model API key in .env
Explicit README warning that this is a consolation build, not a production replacement
whatYouLose: licensed data, avatars, and production templates
high-fidelity color, format, and export handling
whyPeopleStillPay: Hailuo AI: The visible editor is small; the value sits in the model, inference capacity, safety controls, and production-quality outputs.
ongoingBurden: Own compute costs, queueing, model and codec changes, consent controls, moderation, storage, and failed jobs.

alternatives.name: ComfyUI
alternatives.desc: The local video ecosystem's engine room; capable of almost anything, friendly to almost nobody at first.

facts.install: Windows or macOS desktop installer, Windows portable archive, or manual Python install on Windows, macOS, or Linux
facts.engines: Local and downloadable image, video, audio, 3D, and text models including Stable Diffusion/SDXL/SD3.5, FLUX, Wan, LTX-Video, HunyuanVideo, CogVideoX, and Mochi; optional API nodes connect to hosted providers
facts.dataFormat: Models, inputs, outputs, and workflow JSON live in the local ComfyUI data tree; generated media can embed workflow and seed metadata, while API nodes transmit selected inputs to their provider
facts.gapVsPaid: It cannot reproduce Hailuo's proprietary MiniMax video model or cloud render speed, and getting comparable motion requires finding and wiring a compatible local workflow.
facts.setupBlocker: A compatible GPU, enough VRAM and disk for multi-gigabyte models, and a working model/workflow must be chosen before useful output appears

alternatives.name: Draw Things
alternatives.desc: Local image-to-video and text-to-video on Apple hardware; slower than a cloud fleet, cheaper than one.

facts.install: Install the signed app from Apple's App Store on macOS, iPhone, or iPad
facts.engines: Runs supported Stable Diffusion, SDXL, FLUX, and video models locally, including imported checkpoints and LoRAs; optional cloud compute can offload generation
facts.dataFormat: Projects, models, history, and generated media live in the app sandbox; on macOS model files are under the app container, while cloud offload sends prompts and media for processing
facts.gapVsPaid: Its available local video models are not Hailuo's MiniMax model, and Apple-device rendering is markedly slower and more memory-bound than Hailuo's cloud.
facts.setupBlocker: Apple hardware is required, and the first model download is large; older devices can be slow or memory-limited

alternatives.name: LTX Desktop
alternatives.desc: A real local video editor with text and image generation built in; your GPU replaces the credit card.

facts.install: Download the Windows .exe or macOS .dmg from the project's GitHub Releases page
facts.engines: LTX video models and bundled image-generation components, with optional LTX API and other configured hosted services; local generation is primarily supported on NVIDIA Windows systems
facts.dataFormat: Projects, settings, logs, downloaded models, source assets, and renders live in the platform-specific LTXDesktop application-data folder; API mode uploads the material needed for the requested generation
facts.gapVsPaid: It substitutes LTX models for Hailuo's MiniMax model, so the characteristic motion and quality differ even before the user confronts the demanding local GPU requirement or API bill.
facts.setupBlocker: Serious local generation currently needs a high-end NVIDIA Windows GPU and very large model downloads; macOS generation relies on an API key instead of local inference

alternatives.name: NodeTool
alternatives.desc: Local video models inside a node canvas and timeline; 450 stars, but the project is very much awake.

facts.install: Install the macOS .dmg, signed Windows .exe, or Linux AppImage; Docker Compose is available for self-hosting
facts.engines: Local Ollama, llama.cpp/GGUF, MLX, Nunchaku, Hugging Face, and diffusion/media models, plus BYOK providers such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, FAL, Replicate, KIE, ElevenLabs, and Hugging Face
facts.dataFormat: Workflows, projects, assets, files, provider settings, and vector indexes live locally in YAML, SQLite/SQLite-vec, and application storage; optional S3 or Supabase storage is supported, and cloud nodes transmit their inputs
facts.gapVsPaid: It can orchestrate local or BYOK models but does not include Hailuo's proprietary MiniMax model or its tuned prompt-to-video experience.
facts.setupBlocker: No useful model or provider is bundled: the user must add an API key or download a multi-gigabyte local model, and some local backends add a large Python/Conda environment

alternatives.name: SwarmUI
alternatives.desc: Text-to-video and image-to-video through a simpler Generate tab, with current local models underneath.

facts.install: Run the Windows installer script, the Linux launch script, or install .NET/Python/Homebrew prerequisites and run launch-macos.sh on macOS; Docker is optional
facts.engines: Uses ComfyUI as its main backend for Stable Diffusion, SDXL, FLUX, Wan, LTX, MiniMax, ACE-Step, and other image/video/audio workflows; an Automatic1111-compatible backend is optional
facts.dataFormat: Configuration, users, models, workflows, generated media, and history live in the local SwarmUI installation and configured model/output directories
facts.gapVsPaid: It offers local model flexibility but not Hailuo's model or one-click cloud rendering, and video workflows become much more technical.
facts.setupBlocker: The backend and models still have to be downloaded, and non-Windows installs require command-line prerequisites such as .NET, Python, and Git

alternatives.name: WanGP
alternatives.desc: A local video workbench for modest GPUs; free to run, not open-source despite the homepage wording.

facts.install: Run the supplied Windows install.bat or Linux/macOS install.sh script; community launchers such as Pinokio are optional
facts.engines: Local video, image, music, speech, and restoration models including Wan, MiniMax/Hailuo-family weights where available, LTX, Hunyuan, LongCat, Qwen Image, Z-Image, FLUX, ACE-Step, and Qwen TTS
facts.dataFormat: Downloaded models, presets, queues, galleries, generated media, and metadata live in the local installation tree and chosen output folders
facts.gapVsPaid: It can run downloadable video models without credits, but it does not reproduce Hailuo's current proprietary service and render speed is capped by the user's GPU.
facts.setupBlocker: Installation must match the GPU and PyTorch/CUDA/ROCm stack, and useful models consume many gigabytes of disk and substantial VRAM

notes: Credibility row: Hailuo AI survives for a structural reason, not because its interface is difficult to copy.
prompt:
Build the closest honest consolation tool inspired by Hailuo AI; do not claim to replace its structural moat.
Use exactly this stack: Python 3.12 + FastAPI + FFmpeg + React.
Primary job: Build the closest honest personal AI video generation workflow using one user-selected local or API model, job history, preview, and export.
Start from an empty folder and create the complete working project.
Make the default mode single-user and private.
Store user data locally unless the core job requires the declared self-hosted database.
Do not add analytics, telemetry, ads, or third-party accounts.
Put every secret and external credential in .env and provide .env.example.
Use realistic sample data that is clearly labelled and easy to delete.
Implement the smallest polished interface that completes the core loop end to end.
Include clear empty, loading, validation, success, and failure states.
Add import and export so the user is not trapped in the app.
Use accessible keyboard navigation, labels, focus states, and sensible contrast.
Validate untrusted input and never log secrets or private file contents.
Deliberately exclude these paid-product advantages: licensed data, avatars, and production templates; high-fidelity color, format, and export handling; frontier generation quality.
Do not fake integrations, network effects, proprietary data, model quality, compliance, or security claims.
Where an external API is optional, keep the app useful without it and explain the degraded mode.
Write focused unit tests for the data model and the most important workflow.
Add one end-to-end smoke test that proves the core loop works.
Create a README with setup, permissions, architecture, data location, backup, and limitations.
Add scripts for install, development, test, build, and a production-style local run.
Run the tests and build before finishing, then fix errors rather than merely describing them.
